case_name: Ruben H. Domdom, Jr. v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: U.S. citizen; worked as port engineer in Iraq for T-Solutions May 23, 2014 - August 21, 2015; claimed dependency exemptions for three children living in Nevada.

adjustments: disallowed section 911 foreign earned income exclusion for each year
section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty for each year
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Entitlement to foreign earned income exclusion (tax home in Iraq) and penalties
conceded: Petitioner: exclusion for each year was improperly computed and overstated

findings_of_fact.fact: Employed in Iraq by T-Solutions from May 23, 2014 until August 21, 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: That employment lasted from May 23, 2014, until August 21, 2015, when he left Iraq to begin working in Alexandria, Egypt.

findings_of_fact.fact: Wages deposited to U.S. bank account; not subject to Iraqi income tax
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner’s wages were not subject to Iraqi income tax for either year in issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: Leased San Diego condominium both years; stored belongings and two cars near San Diego
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner leased a two -bedroom condominium in San Diego during both years in issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: Purchased Nevada house in 2014 where former spouse and three children lived
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2014 petitioner purchased a Nevada single -family house. His former spouse and three of their children lived there during the years in issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: Returns claimed head of household and dependency exemptions for three children; Las Vegas addresses
findings_of_fact.snippet: each return shows his filing status as head of household. Petitioner claimed dependency exemption deduction s for three of his children for both

findings_of_fact.fact: Stipulated: met 330-day physical presence test each year
findings_of_fact.snippet: The parties have stipulated that for each year in issue petitioner met the 330 -day physical presence test under section 911(d)(1).

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner did not establish that his abode was not within the United States
findings_of_fact.snippet: Because petitioner has not establi shed that his abode was not within the United States for either year in issue

findings_of_fact.fact: Underpayments exceed greater of $5,000 or 10% of tax required to be shown; written supervisory approval obtained
findings_of_fact.snippet: they exceed the greater of $5,000 or 10% of the amount s of tax required to have been shown on petitioner’s 2014 and 2015 returns

findings_of_fact.fact: Disclosed wages on Form 2555; returns prepared by paid preparer given W-2s and employment facts; reasonable reliance found
findings_of_fact.snippet: We find that petitioner reas onably relied on the advice of his return preparer with respect to the application of section 911(a)

issues.question: Other (foreign earned income exclusion §911): may petitioner exclude wages earned in Iraq in 2014 and 2015, i.e., was his tax home in a foreign country given §911(d)(3)'s abode rule?
issues.holding: Not entitled: petitioner failed to establish that his abode was not within the United States, so under §911(d)(3) he cannot have a foreign tax home; exclusion denied both years
issues.computable_reason: Given the finding that abode outside the U.S. was not established, §911(d)(3) mechanically bars a foreign tax home and thus the exclusion; the abode finding itself is a facts-and-circumstances judgment.

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalties for 2014 and 2015?
issues.holding: Not liable: although understatements were substantial and supervisory approval obtained, petitioner had reasonable cause and acted in good faith by relying on his paid preparer
issues.computable_reason: Decided on reasonable cause / reliance on preparer.

decision.text: An appropriate order and decision will be entered.
decision.summary: Foreign earned income exclusion denied for 2014 and 2015; no section 6662(a) penalties.

notes: Deficiency and penalty amounts not stated in opinion. Respondent's oral motion to conform pleadings (to put HOH status at issue) was denied; HOH eligibility not before the Court but used inferentially as inconsistent with foreign abode. 7491(a) not applicable.
